title: Per-dispatch stage timeout with orch-sequential retirement
goal: Kill every hung run hook at its per-stage limit on every dispatch route, end it timed_out, and retire the orch-sequential backend that silently discards the limit it is given

steps.description: Write RED tests for stage_timeout_s core behaviour (must FAIL before implementation): (a) hung `run` hook is terminated at its limit on a direct dispatch; (b) whole process group dies — a child ignoring TERM leaves nothing after TERM + 10 s; (c) precedence template > ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S > 90 min; (d) loader rejects stage_timeout_s below router.timeout_s and non-integer; (e) each retry and each map member gets a fresh timer; (f) always_run stage reads stage_timeout_s, not router.timeout_s; (g) missing backend → misconfigured event; (h) guard: orch-sequential plugin dir absent + no non-adr file names it; (i) a plan dispatch longer than 300 s inside its stage_timeout_s completes (flat backend timeout no longer undercuts it).

Amend ADR-054 §9, ADR-017, and ADR-011 with new statements and ## Enforced by sections. ADR-054 §9: add stage_timeout_s, its 3-tier precedence, the 90-min default, the loader rule (≥ router.timeout_s), the timed_out disposition, and the per-dispatch-timer guarantee. ADR-017: state router.timeout_s bounds one model call only; always_run stages move to stage_timeout_s. ADR-011: orch-sequential retired; default backend is bash-parallel; missing or unreadable backend is misconfigured, not a fallback. Remove ADR-011 and ADR-017 from config/adr-enforcement-baseline.txt (shrinks by 2 lines per the ONLY-SHRINKS rule).

Parse and validate stage_timeout_s in core/pipeline/template.sh. In the AWK stage-row parser, capture a new `stage_timeout_s` scalar alongside `router.timeout_s`. Store in _TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_<safe_id> for every stage (always_run stages included). Validate at load time: must be a positive integer; must be ≥ the same stage's router.timeout_s (error if not). Apply env fallback ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S and engine default 5400 when the template field is absent. Add template_stage_timeout_s() getter mirroring template_stage_router_timeout().

Implement per-dispatch timer in plugin_hook_call for the `run` hook. After sourcing the plugin subshell, run it under `set -m` (makes it a process group leader) in the background; arm a watchdog that calls zbuild_pg_kill TERM then KILL after 10 s grace. Read stage_timeout_s from _TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_<stage> → ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S → 5400. Cancel the watchdog when the hook exits normally. On timeout expiry: write a timed_out result disposition naming the stage and the limit (using the existing _verdict_write_result / disposition layer), emit plugin.run.timed_out event. The watchdog itself gets set -m so cancelling it leaves no sleep behind. Source scripts/lib/proc-group.sh lazily (same fail-open pattern as the other module loads in the function). Each retry and each map member dispatch is a separate plugin_hook_call invocation so each gets a fresh timer by construction.

Fix _runner_dispatch_always_run in runner.sh: read _TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_<safe> instead of _TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_<safe> for the dispatch time limit. Replace the hand-rolled ( set -m; kill -TERM -- -$pid; sleep 2; kill -KILL ) watchdog with zbuild_pg_kill (TERM → KILL, default 10 s grace). The outer subshell + set -m wrapper that creates the always_run stage's group is retained per the existing #2333 comment. Source scripts/lib/proc-group.sh if not already loaded.

Fix _orch_local_collect_results and _orch_local_shutdown_pool in core/orch/local_engine.sh to use zbuild_pg_kill / zbuild_pid_kill. Replace _orch_local_kill_slot (single-PID kills, 0.5 s grace) with zbuild_pg_kill where the pid can be resolved to a distinct group, falling back to zbuild_pid_kill. Source scripts/lib/proc-group.sh. Grace time changes from 0.5 s to 10 s per Decision 2. _orch_local_kill_slot may be removed or kept only for the test-stage registration path if it still uses it.

Remove the flat ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT from all three strategy files. In each, replace `orch_collect "$pool_id" --timeout "${ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT:-300}"` with `orch_collect "$pool_id"` (no timeout arg). The per-dispatch timer in plugin_hook_call is now the only stage limit; a plan dispatch longer than 300 s and inside its stage_timeout_s must complete. Also remove any ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT export/documentation in these files.

Retire orch-sequential. (a) Delete plugins/tool/orch-sequential/ (manifest.yaml, plugin.sh, tests/orch-sequential-test.sh) and tests/golden/orch-sequential-capabilities.golden and docs/wiki/plugins/orch-sequential.md (guard test in step-1 would flag this if left). Update docs/wiki/Plugins.md to remove the orch-sequential row. (b) In core/orch/contract.sh: remove the two fallback-to-sequential paths in orch_load_backend (the explicit `backend == sequential` branch and the general fallback); replace them with a hard misconfigured error emitting an orch.backend.misconfigured event naming the backend alias. In _orch_load_backend: change default from sequential to bash-parallel; discard `2>/dev/null || true` (missing backend is now fatal). Add an explicit check that rejects alias values `sequential` and `orch-sequential` as misconfigured. (c) Migrate existing unit tests that used orch-sequential as a fixture to orch-mock: summary-mandatory-test.sh, dispatch-rc-guard-test.sh, stdin-spawn-guard-test.sh, core-orch-run-id-isolation-test.sh, adr059-no-tmpdir-defaults-test.sh, plugin-artifact-goldens-test.sh — swap the source/plugin path and alias to orch-mock.

Add stage_timeout_s values to config/templates/simple.yaml per the measured-and-rounded table in the issue: test 90 m (5400 s), build 70 m (4200 s), design 65 m (3900 s), plan 20 m (1200 s), test-author 15 m (900 s), acceptance-gate / issue-acceptance / spec-coverage / spec-correspondence / review_lenses 10 m (600 s), all others (intake, pr, hydrate, secret-scan, shape-floor, design-gate, gate-aggregator, assertion-integrity, review-aggregator) 10 m (600 s). Move always_run stages release and persist from router.timeout_s to stage_timeout_s at their current values (release: 30 s, persist: 120 s). Do NOT add router.timeout_s to always_run stages; that key now means only one model call. Verify the loader accepts every value (stage_timeout_s ≥ router.timeout_s for every stage that declares both).

notes:
1. TIMED_OUT DISPOSITION WRITE PATH: plugin_hook_call must write the timed_out word to the stage result AFTER killing the plugin subshell. The existing disposition layer (_verdict_write_result / core/pipeline/verdict.sh / core/pipeline/disposition.sh) must be checked for the exact call shape before implementing step-4. Hand-writing a partial JSON would violate the 'data another part of the engine writes is checked against its writer' rule (CLAUDE.md). This is the largest gap in the plan and deserves a careful read of those files at the start of step-4.
2. SET -M IN PLUGIN_HOOK_CALL: plugin_hook_call is currently called from inside the runner's own shell (not a subprocess). `set -m` is scoped to the plugin subshell `( ... ) &`, not to the runner. This is structurally safe. The watchdog must be in the same scope so zbuild_pg_kill can reference the plugin's PGID before `wait` returns.
3. GRACE TIME CHANGE: _orch_local_collect_results currently uses 0.5 s; Decision 2 specifies TERM + 10 s. This is a 20× increase for the collect path. It is intentional per the issue.
4. ADR-011 DEFAULT BACKEND IN ADR VS CODE: The code default in config/config.sh is already bash-parallel (issue mentions this gap between code and ADR-011 text). The ADR amendment in step-2 aligns the spec to the code. Verify config/config.sh zbuild_config_get_backend still defaults to bash-parallel after step-8.
5. WIKI DOCS: docs/wiki/plugins/orch-sequential.md must be deleted (guard test fails if it exists and it is not under docs/adr/). docs/wiki/Plugins.md has a row for orch-sequential that must be removed. Both are in step-8.
6. ALWAYS_RUN RELEASE/PERSIST ROUTER.TIMEOUT_S: After step-9, release and persist have stage_timeout_s but no router.timeout_s (they make no model calls). The template loader's validation rule (stage_timeout_s ≥ router.timeout_s) applies only when router.timeout_s is declared; when absent the floor check is a no-op. Verify template.sh implements this correctly.
7. RETRY FRESH TIMER: Each retry of a stage dispatches through plugin_hook_call, so each retry naturally gets a fresh timer. The acceptance criterion is satisfied by construction — no special code needed. The test in step-1 should confirm this empirically by planting a stage that times out on the first attempt and observes the second attempt's timer started fresh.
8. ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT IN TESTS: grep-rl found router-timeout-precedence-e2e-test.sh, router-loop-rc124-honors-sentinel-test.sh, router-retries-test.sh referencing router.timeout_s; these are for the ROUTER setting and are unaffected. Only the three strategy source files pass ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT to orch_collect.
